title: Capacity bottleneck sample extract (april-2026)
summary: Ad-hoc data pull to isolate a regional capacity bottleneck observed during a mid-Apr 2026 traffic spike. This sheet contains raw query snippets, extraction logic, sample CSV rows, quick charts to copy into Looker, and open questions for follow-up. Intended for SRE + infra ownership handoff and to feed the wider postmortem.
body:
Context:
- Incident window: 2026-04-14 09:30 - 2026-04-14 12:10 UTC (customer reports + internal SLO alerts).
- Symptom: sudden increase in request queue length for hosted-api in region eu-west-1, elevated GPU saturations on a subset of N1 nodes, and progressive throttling on the service tier.
- Hypothesis: uneven shard placement + long-tail sequence jobs caused local queuing and throttles; autoscaler did not provision due to tight commit thresholds.

Primary objectives for this extract:
1) Show 1-minute and 5-minute queue length distributions by host and az.
2) Correlate per-host GPU_util% with per-request service time and KV cache hit ratio.
3) Identify top 20 request routes causing the highest queue growth and their model variants.
4) Generate per-region throttle histogram and earliest throttle timestamp for each customer tier.

Data sources used:
- metrics.gpu.node.* (prometheus)
- serving.rpc.queue_length and serving.rpc.latency (tsdb)
- routing.throttle.events (events store)
- job.meta (postgres) for model variant mapping
- s3://redwood-logs/hosted-api/eu-west-1/2026-04-14/*.parquet (request traces)

Extraction queries (SQL / pseudo-SQL to reproduce):
- "-- 1min queue length by host
SELECT time_bin(60s, ts) AS minute, host, avg(queue_length) AS q_len_avg, max(queue_length) AS q_len_max FROM serving.rpc.queue_length WHERE region = 'eu-west-1' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-04-14 09:00' AND '2026-04-14 13:00' GROUP BY minute, host ORDER BY minute, q_len_max DESC;"
- "-- GPU util + avg service time join
SELECT m.host, time_bin(60s, m.ts) AS minute, avg(m.gpu_util) AS gpu_util_avg, avg(r.service_ms) AS svc_ms_avg, avg(m.kv_cache_hit) AS kv_hit_avg FROM metrics.gpu.node m JOIN serving.rpc.latency r ON r.host = m.host AND time_bin(60s, r.ts) = time_bin(60s, m.ts) WHERE m.region = 'eu-west-1' AND m.ts BETWEEN '2026-04-14 09:00' AND '2026-04-14 13:00' GROUP BY m.host, minute ORDER BY gpu_util_avg DESC;"
- "-- Top routes by queue delta
WITH q AS (SELECT time_bin(60s, ts) AS minute, route, sum(queue_length) AS q FROM serving.rpc.queue_length WHERE region = 'eu-west-1' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-04-14 09:00' AND '2026-04-14 13:00' GROUP BY minute, route) SELECT route, max(q) AS peak_q, (max(q) - min(q)) AS q_delta FROM q GROUP BY route ORDER BY q_delta DESC LIMIT 20;"
- "-- Per-customer-tier earliest throttle
SELECT tier, min(ts) AS first_throttle_ts, count(*) AS throttle_count FROM routing.throttle.events WHERE region = 'eu-west-1' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-04-14 09:00' AND '2026-04-14 13:00' GROUP BY tier ORDER BY first_throttle_ts;"

Sample extracted CSV rows (copy/pasteable):
- queue_by_host_minute.csv columns: minute,host,q_len_avg,q_len_max
  2026-04-14T09:31:00Z,eu-n1-003,1.4,6
  2026-04-14T09:32:00Z,eu-n1-007,0.9,3
  2026-04-14T10:12:00Z,eu-n1-003,3.1,12

- gpu_svc_join_sample.csv columns: minute,host,gpu_util_avg,svc_ms_avg,kv_hit_avg
  2026-04-14T10:12:00Z,eu-n1-003,95.6,420,0.12
  2026-04-14T10:12:00Z,eu-n1-007,67.2,220,0.48

Key findings from the extract (quick notes):
- A small subset of hosts (eu-n1-003, eu-n1-011, eu-n1-019) hit >90% GPU_util for sustained 8-15 minute windows coincident with queue_length spikes. These hosts serviced routes dominated by long-sequence generation (avg tokens > 120).
- KV cache hit ratio on the overloaded hosts was low (~10-15%), suggesting little reuse of prefixes for this traffic mix.
- Autoscaler behavior: there were 2 scale-up decisions attempted but blocked by the "available-commit" gate (commit threshold = 0.94). The timeline shows scale decision at 09:37 but no new capacity visible until 10:25 because the region-level allocator favored other zones.
- Throttle events started at 09:44 for standard tier and at 09:49 for free tier; enterprise tier saw few throttles but experienced increased latency via queued requests.

Quick charts to paste into a postmortem doc:
- 1: minute vs max_queue (line chart) over incident window (annotate autoscaler decisions)
- 2: host GPU_util stacked bar for top 5 hosts (peak minute)
- 3: route heatmap (route x minute) showing queue intensity
- 4: throttle_count by tier (bar) with first_throttle_ts table beside it

Open questions / follow-ups (actionable):
- Why did the allocator not assign the new compute to eu-west-1 AZs where the load was concentrated? Follow-up owners: Samira (allocator infra), Priya (autoscaler). Ticket: JIRA-ENG-4821.
- Are the long-sequence routes coming from a small set of customers (high-variance behavior) or many customers concurrently? Need a customer-id breakdown (pull from request traces). Owner: Jordan.
- Should we lower the commit threshold temporarily when queue_length > 8 for > 5 minutes? Risk: flapping and cost. Prepare a canary policy. Owner: Alex.
- Explore whether prefix caching policy could be warmed for heavy long-sequence traffic (prefetch heuristics). Owner: Research/Applied-ML.

Notes to self / replication tips:
- Use parquet_snappy extraction from S3, then run above SQL in our clickhouse replica (schema: serving.rpc.* mapped to s3 materialized tables).
- For faster joins, pre-aggregate metrics.gpu.node to 60s bins and push into temp table.
- When sharing charts with PMs, include both queue_length and gpu_util on dual axis to avoid confusion.

Appendix: quick timeline (derived from extracted events)
- 09:30 UTC: traffic ramp begins in eu-west-1 (external load + a few customer test jobs).
- 09:37 UTC: autoscaler signals desired_add = 6 but commit gate blocks (threshold 0.94).
- 09:44 UTC: first standard-tier throttle events (routing.throttle.events).
- 10:02 UTC: peak queue observed on eu-n1-003 (q_len_max = 18).
- 10:12 UTC: sustained GPU util >90% window begins for 3 hosts.
- 10:25 UTC: additional capacity finally assigned to region (partial relief).
- 11:05 UTC: throttles taper, latency returns near baseline.

Contact / next steps:
- Draft a short postmortem outline and circulate to infra + SRE; include this extract as the data appendix.
- Schedule a follow-up sync week of 2026-04-22 to decide guardrail changes.

Unresolved caveats:
- Sampling bias: S3 traces have a 1:10 sample in this pipeline for non-enterprise customers; counts may underrepresent tail behavior. Mark any customer-count-based conclusions as tentative.
- Metric clock skew: nodes sometimes report with ±3s skew; use 60s bins to mitigate.

Relevant links: JIRA-ENG-4821 (allocator), confluence/capacity-playbook (for commit thresholds), internal slack thread #infra-incident-2026-04-14.
